title: fed: direct address delivery MUST NOT substitute for mailbox path
description: Direct address security section says 'Senders MUST NOT treat successful delivery to a directAddress as a substitute for mailbox delivery' and 'The standard mailbox path MUST always be used.' These are sender-side implementation obligations that the receiving server cannot verify or enforce. A sender that skips mailbox delivery is misbehaving, but the receiver has no visibility into whether mailbox delivery also occurred. Decision: downgrade both to SHOULD NOT / SHOULD, acknowledging these are best-practice obligations on the sender.
close_reason: Downgraded MUST NOT/MUST to SHOULD NOT/SHOULD — both are sender-side obligations the receiver cannot observe or enforce. Rationale text unchanged.
